name: Services
pullQuote: Facilities work is noticed only when it stops. That is the standard.
overview: The services business looks after buildings and the institutions inside them. It is the least visible of the group's sectors and the closest to daily life — the work that decides whether a school, a hospital or an office is a decent place to spend a day, and which is noticed almost exclusively in its absence.

Institutional care sits alongside general facilities work because the two demand the same thing: continuity. Buildings in constant public use cannot be taken offline for convenience, so the work has to happen around the people using them.

approach.heading: Around the people using the building
body: Everything is scheduled around occupancy rather than around the crew. That is slower and more awkward than the alternative, and it is the only way to maintain a building genuinely in use without degrading the thing the building is for.

Continuity of people matters as much as continuity of service. Teams that stay with a site learn its particular faults — the door that drops in humidity, the plant that needs attention before anything registers — and that knowledge does not survive being handed over.
